sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA

ON THE 4 th OF DECEMBER, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 8680 of 2020  RAJESH  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Mr. Vipin Babu Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Abhishek Bhadoriya - Govt. Advocate for responden  ORDER

The present petition under Section 528 of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) has been filed for the deletion of the phrase "benefit of doubt," which was mentioned in the order of the Revisional Court passed in Special Sessions Trial No. 193 of 2013, even though the petitioner was acquitted.
Counsel for the petitioner submits that he was earlier acquitted of the charges under Sections 450,
376, and 506 Part II of the IPC by the Revisional Court.
Even though the acquittal was recorded, in paragraph 18, a phrase, 'benefit of doubt' has been mentioned, which adversely affects his future.
In support of his contention, he has relied upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajbir Vs, State of Haryana , reported i n 1985 (Supp) SCC 272 .

entities.text: Rajbir Vs, State of Haryana , reported i n 1985 (Supp) SCC 272
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In such circumstances,
he prayed for a direction that this phrase may be deleted, or that the court clarify the phrase will not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31506 2 MCRC-8680-2020 affect his future.
On the other hand, counsel for the State has supported the impugned order and prayed for its dismissal.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Upon perusal of the record, it is seen that, in paragraph 7 of the impugned order, Aman Ahirwar admitted to an illicit relationship between his wife and the accused.
He further stated that she met with the accused, Rajesh, in his absence.
The case relied upon by the counsel for the petitioner is of no help, as the facts found in that case are different; therefore, it is distinguishable.
In such circumstances, the Revisional Court rightly observed that the accused was acquitted of the charges, primarily on the benefit of doubt.
Therefore, no interference is warranted in the present facts and circumstances.
